paragraphs: Swamiji loved a charming Indian fable about oysters and pearls. According to it, when rain falls while the star Svati is high in the sky, any drop that lands inside an oyster turns into a pearl.

The oysters, the fable says, know this secret. So when that star shines, they rise to the surface of the sea and wait with their shells open for that precious drop. The moment one falls in, they snap their shells shut and dive to the sea floor. There, in the quiet depths, they patiently work on the drop until it becomes a pearl.

Swamiji said we should do the same with a great idea. First hear it, then understand it. After that, close yourself off from distractions and outside noise, and give yourself fully to growing that truth inside you.

He warned against a common trap: wasting your energy by grabbing an idea just because it is new, then dropping it as soon as something newer comes along. Pick one thing, carry it through, and see it to the end. Don't quit before you get there.

Only the person who can become completely absorbed in an idea finds real light, he said. Those who nibble a little here and a little there get a brief thrill, and nothing more. They stay at the mercy of their senses and never rise beyond them.
learn: In a world of endless tabs, new courses and new trends, depth is rare and valuable. Choose one worthwhile goal, protect it from distraction, and stay with it long enough for it to become your pearl.
